title: Error correlation improved joint ENSO probability scores at four leads for 2000-2024 origins
abstract: We tested joint uncertainty for Nino 3.4 monthly temperature forecasts at leads of 3, 6, 9 and 12 months. Both rules had the same earlier-only mean forecasts and seasonal marginal variances. The test used an error correlation matrix from earlier complete forecast vectors, with 10% shrinkage toward independence. Across 300 monthly origins in 2000-2024, mean joint negative log density fell from 3.71919 to 2.50241 nats. The gain was 1.21678 nats, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of 0.99407 to 1.45578. For the equal mean of the four target months, nominal 90% coverage rose from 70.67% to 88.67%, with wider intervals and lower interval score. Fixed shrinkage and calibration checks retained positive joint-score gains. This supports a known covariance method in this benchmark. It does not identify a physical cause or show improvement over operational ENSO systems. Revised NOAA inputs, one model, Gaussian distributions, overlapping targets and 25 test years limit inference. Code, exact external provenance, aggregate evidence, a numerical audit and reproduction steps are included.
